title: The hearths of Àth dhearg take the tower on half-pay
summary: The custodian of Àth dhearg calls the town's hearths to the room over the net-store. A' Chompanaidh will pay half the cost of a tower on the north-eastern cape in marks and send the lens and oil; the town is to find the stone and the hands, the other half of the pay being the promise that the light will bring its boats home. The town agrees.

title: Torcall's cairn set in the footing of the tower
summary: The masons of Àth dhearg raise the tower over the old fire-shelf on the cape. They take down the cairn Torcall Clachair built there with James Fenn and set its stones in the footing, facing the sea, and turn a stair inside the wall. The old cut stair up the cliff is left as it was.

title: The first line of the Àth dhearg daybook
summary: On the night of the lighting Tormod mac Pheadair, keeper of Taigh-solais Àth dhearg, writes the first line in the grey-bound book of the humans' paper that A' Chompanaidh left him: lit at dusk, the wind west and light, and no ship. It is the first keeper's daybook kept on the island.

title: Two dates at the head of the daybook
summary: A man of A' Chompanaidh, unable to tell the days of passing ships from the nights of the moon, writes out the humans' months for the keeper of Àth dhearg. Thereafter Tormod mac Pheadair heads every entry with the humans' day above and the night of the moon beneath, and writes the humans' days in over his first entries.

title: The Àth dhearg boats brought home in the Bealltach gale
summary: A north-easterly gale catches four boats of Àth dhearg on the long lines beyond the reef. The keeper lights the lamp an hour before dusk. Three boats come home by the light through the night, one from the wrong side of the reef; the fourth returns at dawn a man short. Tormod mac Pheadair enters the boats and the lost man by name.

title: The masons' pay entered in the roll of Àth dhearg
summary: When A' Chompanaidh pays the eleven masons of the tower in marks at its foot, the custodian's clerk enters the payment in the town's roll, and beside it that the other half of their pay was made in the Bealltach gale, in four boats and three of them home.

title: The keeper of Àth dhearg sees the burning collier
summary: Two nights after entering a laden collier of A' Chompanaidh going south, Tormod mac Pheadair sees a red light low in the south under the cloud from the middle watch until near dawn, and writes that he does not know what it was. The carters bring word four days later that raiders have burned her.

title: The collier's crew fed near Ceann leathan
summary: The raiders who burn the collier of A' Chompanaidh put her crew into their own boat and set them rowing for the land. The crew come ashore alive at a fishing village near Ceann leathan, where the households feed and shelter them until a rider can carry word south to Seann Bhral.

title: A' Chompanaidh charges Comann an Airgid with the burning
summary: Within a month of the burning the agents of A' Chompanaidh say at Seann Bhral and Ros dhomhain, and write to Arthur Lisle, that Comann an Airgid paid the raiders in spite for the surveyors turned back from the adit at Muileann chiar. The guild makes no answer.

title: The keeper will not write the black boats
summary: In Dubhlas a clerk of A' Chompanaidh rides to Àth dhearg to read the daybook and asks the keeper to write in black raiding boats seen going south before the burning. Tormod mac Pheadair answers that he saw none and will write no boat he has not seen. The clerk reports the book of no assistance.

title: The gunboat entered at Àth dhearg
summary: In Teasach of the forty-seventh year a black two-masted ship of war of A' Chompanaidh, a gun in her bows under canvas and more men on deck than any trader carries, comes round the north coast and south past the cape. The keeper of Àth dhearg enters her with more care than any ship before.

title: Àth dhearg lends two boats to Ceann leathan
summary: A fisherman of Ceann leathan walks north nearly forty miles with two sons to ask Àth dhearg for a boat after the gunboat burns the cove. The households talk into the night and lend two, to be returned when Ceann leathan has built its own, and the three sail them south in Lùghnas.

title: The wall's footing on the shingle of Baile dhìreach
summary: Promised timber by A' Chompanaidh, the yard-master Daniel Lusk asks the council of four at Baile dhìreach for a dry-stone wall up the town's shingle and lays its footing while they argue. The town's members hold that the shingle is kept and not built on. On the third night the stones are carried below the wrack-line.

title: The shingle clause read from both books
summary: Nathan Cobb reads the compact of Baile dhìreach from the humans' book, where the shingle is the town's property; Iain Hale reads it from the Dia-thìris book, where the shingle is kept for the town. Asked by both sides which book is right, Iain Hale closes the book and says nothing.

title: The Hales keep their house at Baile dhìreach
summary: When the council breaks and the human families leave for Ros bheag and Ros dhomhain, Samuel Hale, Eilidh nic Ruairidh and their son Iain stay in their house by the well at the head of the street. They take neither side on the wall and speak of other things when it is mentioned.

title: Iain Hale refuses the yard at Inis chrom
summary: Daniel Lusk offers Iain Hale the foreman's place in the yard going to Inis chrom, for more marks than the yard has ever paid. After a night on the shingle and a talk with his father, Iain Hale refuses, and that winter builds the town's boats on the old slip by the town's leave.

title: The humans' book set back on the shelf
summary: When the yard has sailed for Inis chrom, Iain Hale finds the council's book in the humans' tongue left open on the mending-table in the net-loft at Baile dhìreach, at a page with a date and nothing under it. He closes it and sets it back on the shelf beside the Dia-thìris book.

title: The rain fails in the Àth dhearg daybook
summary: Through the spring and summer of the forty-eighth year the daybook of Àth dhearg records dry winds night after night, the fields inland yellow before midsummer, a heath fire of three days, and the burn below the town stopped, which it has never done in memory. Rain is written once in four months.

title: Tormod mac Pheadair reads the seed loan at Baile ruadh
summary: Called by his wife's kin, the keeper of Àth dhearg walks to Baile ruadh and reads to its council, figure by figure, the terms in the humans' figures by which A' Chompanaidh's store at Seann Dunn lends seed corn for grain over five harvests. He finds the figures as the interpreter gave them.

title: Baile ruadh's seed debt entered
summary: The custodians' roll of Baile ruadh enters the town's debt of seed corn to A' Chompanaidh under the night of the moon, with the measure and the five harvests, the first debt in grain to the strangers in any roll of the island. The clerk writes beside it the name of the keeper who read the figures.
